changes: See and manage the folders all your devices follow, from any of them. Subscriptions lists each of your computers, and you can pause, resume, change or stop what another computer (or a server) keeps in sync, as long as it allows remote control.

A computer can keep its downloads folder to itself, so your other devices can only save into its named destinations, like Movies and TV on a media server. Turn off “Into the downloads folder too” under Settings › Downloads (communal remote downloads off on a server).
Someone who shares with everyone on a hub can now be asked to connect straight from the Library, without searching for them under People first.
Devices show an icon for what they are (Mac, Windows, Linux or Android) in the Library, Settings › Devices and Subscriptions. This needs your hub to be updated too.
Long file names no longer spill over the rest of a row in Search, Browse and Transfers; the full name shows when you point at it.
Communal remembers the size and place of its window after a restart.
AI assistants can manage destinations, remote control and other devices’ subscriptions, read part of a file, wait for a download to finish, and explain why someone can or can’t see something.
On Android: a computer’s destinations and the folders it keeps in sync show up, setup fields stay above the keyboard, and hidden dotfiles are left out.

Communal for Android: find files, download them to your phone, and keep folders in sync, like music from your computer. Your phone joins your account with a code from Settings › Devices › Add a computer, and only downloads: it never shares its own files. Get the app from the release page; it tells you about new versions. This needs your hub to be updated too.

Your devices can download for each other. From your phone, another computer or the communal command, ask one of your computers to download a file, download or follow a folder, or show and cancel its downloads, so things are waiting there when you get back. Turn it on for each computer under Settings › Downloads (communal remote allow on a server). This needs your hub to be updated too.

Destinations: give folders names like Movies, TV or Music under Settings › Downloads, then pick them under the arrow next to Download or in the folder dialogs. Your other devices can only save into a computer's named destinations, never anywhere else.
Downloading a big folder no longer stops for five minutes partway through. This needs your hub to be updated too.
Adding a computer no longer waits forever when the computer approving it knows your hub by a different address.
In the synced folder, editing a file on one computer while it’s being deleted on another no longer leaves two copies of it on both.

Transfers and Activity have a Clear button. Clearing Transfers removes finished downloads from the list; the files stay where they are. Clearing Activity forgets who got files from this computer, after asking.

Hubs now protect themselves from being flooded: they limit how many new accounts one internet address can create in an hour, how many files one computer can share and how many computers one account can have. If you run a hub, change these under Settings › Hubs › Manage › Settings › Limits. This needs your hub to be updated too.
Names that use hidden characters to look like someone else's, or to disguise a file's real extension, are no longer accepted, and downloaded files are saved without those characters.

If you run a hub, you can now manage it from the app: Settings › Hubs › Manage. Let in people who are waiting, ban and unban, rename the hub, choose whether new people need approval, see who's connected to whom, and read a log of every admin action. The first person to join a hub is its admin. This needs your hub to be updated too.
When someone is waiting to join a hub you manage, a banner says so.
Someone you know on several hubs is listed once in People, with what's going on with them on each hub.
Quitting Communal now shows your computer as offline to others straight away, instead of after a minute and a half. This needs your hub to be updated too.
Saving a download into one of your shared folders shares it as well. Communal now tells you who will be able to see it, and asks first.
Settings › Account explains why your first computer and your recovery key need looking after.
AI assistants can look at thumbnails, check what a change to who-can-see-what would do before making it, check where a download would be shared, and help manage a hub you run.
Long folder paths no longer push the buttons next to them out of view.
Downloading a folder of many files no longer pauses after every few files. When the computer sending them is busy, the next file starts as soon as one finishes.
My shares shows each folder once, with who can see it right on the folder. Change files and folders inside with Files inside…. If you're on several hubs, each hub gets its own line.
People shows which of your connections are online, and when the others were last around. This needs your hub to be updated too.
A green shield follows the name of everyone you've verified, wherever their name appears.
Search can show only files from your connections, or only from people you've verified.
Hubs can have a name, set by whoever runs the hub. The app shows it instead of the hub's address.
Download has a menu with Save to…, instead of a separate button.
The synced folder no longer copies its .communal-sync file between computers.
On Linux, install or update with one command: curl -fsSL https://hypnopompia.github.io/Communal/install.sh | sh

A synced folder: turn it on in My shares on each of your computers and it stays the same on all of them. Only you can see it. Files you add, change or delete follow on the others, and deleted files go to the trash. If you were already keeping a folder named Communal in step by hand, it becomes your synced folder by itself.
When the same file was changed on two computers before they could sync, both versions are kept: the newer one under its name, the other as a "conflicted copy".
Choose where downloads go in Settings › Downloads, or use Save to… next to any Download to pick a folder for that file.
Download a whole folder from the Library, with the folders inside it. Files you already have aren't downloaded again.
Files in a folder you move into a shared folder all at once are now ready to share right away, instead of after a while.

When you're looking at someone's computer (or another of yours) in the Library, new files, removed files and new thumbnails now show up right away. You no longer need to leave and come back. This needs your hub to be updated too.
The Library's list of computers also updates by itself when someone starts or stops sharing with you.
The Library remembers whether you picked grid or list view.
Computers you've removed from your account no longer clutter Settings › Devices. Show them again with the button below the list.
A computer that was removed from your account now says so, and can start over to be added again with a new code. Its old data is kept in a backup folder.
Leaving your last hub now takes you to a screen where you can join one again, instead of an empty window.
Keep a folder in step between two of your own computers: subscribe to it from each one. Files added, changed or deleted on either side show up on the other.
Adding a computer to your account now says clearly that you need to approve it on your other computer, and that computer shows a banner asking you to review it.
When a hub's admin hasn't let you in yet, or a hub refuses this computer, a banner says so instead of just "Not connected".
The app icon no longer looks scrambled at small sizes on Mac.
First release: share folders from your computer with people you know, and download straight from theirs.
Search everything shared with you, with previews of pictures, videos, music, PDFs and text.
Choose who can see each folder or file: only you, particular people or groups, or everyone on a hub.
Follow a friend's folder to get new files automatically.
Let AI assistants such as Claude use Communal for you (Settings › AI agents).
